steps.text: Beat together milk, eggs, sugar, cocoa powder, baking powder, and salt.
Heat a lightly buttered skillet or griddle over medium heat.

Dip each slice of bread into egg mixture until well soaked, about 20 seconds per side. Place in pan, and cook on both sides until they are no longer gooey or shiny in the middle when cut in half, about 3 to 4 minutes per side.

raw_recipe.headline: Chocolate French Toast
raw_recipe.description: Adding cocoa powder to the basic French toast egg mixture turns the classic French toast into something chocolatey and delicious.
raw_recipe.name: Chocolate French Toast

review.reviewBody: Loved the idea, it was perfectly sweet and I could taste the chocolate. Rather than adding cocoa powder to the milk/egg mixture, I just used chocolate milk. Turned out great!

Adjusted the servings to 4, which makes enough for 6 slices of French toast. 

Used a hand mixer and found that the cocoa powder incorporated well. 

Cooked on low heat (stove heat level 3) and each side cooked within 1 minute and 45 seconds. 

Added whipped coconut cream with fresh strawberries and bananas. Delightful!

I made just enough for me (2 pieces): Following advice of others, I combined 1 Tbsp Cocoa (Hershey's Dark) and 2 Tbsp sugar. Then I mixed in 3 Tbsp milk, one Tbsp at a time. Added the egg. I remembered the baking powder but forgot the salt. I cooked them on each side for about 3 minutes and they were great! Very chocolately, but not overly sweet. I have a small whisk that I used to combine the ingredients. I will make this again.
5/29/2016 -- I did make this again. Forgot the salt and the baking powder and don't see that it made any difference. I used a tsp of raspberry jam on top of each piece -- a great addition. This is going to be a staple of Sunday morning breakfast.
June 2016 -- My granddaughter and I made the full recipe for dinner one night. No left overs! Love this recipe!

I made this recipe this past weekend. I saw the reviews about difficulty mixing the cocoa in the mix...I was able to get it mixed in well with a hand held mixer, it took about a minute but got it to work on low to medium speed. the french toast turned out well...not too sweet but just the right amount of sweetness. I also used half and half instead of milk...

My kids love chocolate chip pancakes and this is even easier (and healthier as it turns out!). Be careful to let the excess egg wash drain off before you cook it in a pan or it might be a little mushy in middle. I had some egg batter left over after the kids left so I put it in a remikin dish, tore up pieces of leftover bread and microwaved it for 8 mins on level 4. Guess what??!? I created wonderful servings of chocolate bread pudding which when cooled was a hit after school with a little confectioners sugar or whipped cream. I will make this for sleepovers and be a neighborhood hero or make the bread pudding alternative when we have people over and impress the whole crowd! Next I will experiment with skim milk, a lower egg white/yolk combo, and whole grain breads to find the healthiest version-- maybe even add a tablespoon of flax seed. I highly recommend using egg beaters to fluff up the eggs and mix the cocoa completely into the egg wash. Add cocoa a little at a time at low speed initially or it will create "cocoa smoke" and you'll have more to clean up than eat.

Just made it. For the people complaining about the cocoa not blending with the egg mixture, you need to make a paste of the cocoa, sugar, baking powder and salt with a small amount of milk first. Then once the cocoa has dissolved, add the rest of the milk and whisk to combine well. What I do after all has been combined is pour the mixture through a mesh strainer to remove any egg shells or lumps so you end up with a nice smooth batter. It was actually pretty good, and a nice change from the usual french toast.

I cut the recipe down to 1/4 since I was just feeding myself. I replaced the sugar and cocoa with 2 Tbs of some really nice organic hot (dark) chocolate mix I had on hand, which solved the issue of mixing in the cocoa powder. The bread was 3/4" thick slices from a hearty whole-grain, seed-covered baguette. I normally fry my french toast in coconut oil, but this time I used 1/2 butter for the flavor. The toast came out sweet enough that I just topped it with plain yogurt, and it was fabulous - as well as healthy.
As usual, I had a little of the mixture left over so I scrambled it, with a sprinkle of shredded coconut mixed in. Yummy!

These came out delicious. I just wisked the cocoa and dry ingredients together first, then added wet. Seemed to blend just fine, Maybe letting it set a little bit when mixed and re-mixing may help. I used thicker 7-grain toast and loved it, Just got to cook it on a lower setting and for longer with thick cuts.

The problem that I had was the cocoa powder would not blend in with the remaining ingredients. The first four slices had a thick coating of cocoa powder on them and they were not edible. The remaining slices did not have enough cocoa powder in the batter so they did not have an enough chocolatey flavor. I used a wire whisk in making the batter. My suggestion would be to blend the ingredients in a blender. I was wondering if chocolate syrup could be substituted for the cocoa powder or if chocolate milk could be substituted. Anyway, I will not be trying this recipe again.

Nice recipe. Whenever you try to add a dry ingredient, you must whisk the sugar and cocoa or cinnamon with the eggs first then add the milk little by little or it will all separate and rise to the top

Took a few tries but the issues I had have more to do with instructions or the lack thereof. First, if you just throw the ingredients together the cocoa will clump. Period. To resolve this I mixed the wet ingredients and sifted the cocoa into the dry. Mix up the dry well then whisk them into the wet. Make sure to use an upwards rotation while whisking. This left me with a foamy chocolatey goodness. I used store bought bread because that's what I had and a 15 sec soak per side is almost too much (10 wasn't enough) cooking time was almost spot on but I did reduce the heat (4 out of 10) because the mixture was burning before it cooked all the way through. I also helped presentation to make sure you let the bread drain for a good 10 sec before throwing it in the pan. That way you don't end up with it flowing around the sides. When it did I used the spatula to slide it away. As a side note, leftover mixture does a slightly odd looking but tasty scrambled egg.
We followed the recipe exactly and ate it with chocolate sauce. It was delicious! The mix was a little bit lumpy, and we would have appreciated a reminder or advice on mixing in the cocoa powder.

I love chocolate, I actually put melted chocolate into the custard to add riches and stuffed with some almond chocolate spread and it is absolutely divine and shared with my friends, I certainly will make it again :)

This was a nice idea, but I really didn't taste the chocolate much. I added some Nutella and chocolate syrup for a more chocolatey taste. Dipping the bread for 20 seconds seems a bit too long for me. Also, I'm not quite sure what the purpose of the baking powder was. It didn't seem to add anything. Overall, it tasted good and is a nice change from regular French Toast.

I really liked it, and used a good quality dark cocoa. The cocoa stirred into the mixture really well, and was rich and tasty! Sweet and yummy. I had mine with a little powdered sugar, vanilla yogurt and fresh strawberries. My son sprinkled powdered sugar and squirted a nice amount of maple syrup on his.

This recipe is great! I tried it alongside another recipe and this one was much better, but vanilla may make it better. Mixing was not that hard, just add the cocoa powder to the whisked eggs to form a 'paste', then baking powder, then slowly add the milk and sugar, while maintaining smoothness. Or make a paste from cocoa and oil, then add to whisked eggs, as cocoa is fat soluble. Thank you
This is a fun and simple recipe that can be made without the cocoa powder to prepare basic french toast. I served it with fresh cherries on the side.

I put a little less sugar than the recipe required. The Chocolate French Toast was excellent. Served with a can of cherry pie filling which was also very tasty with the toast. If you like chocolate you will enjoy eating this delicious French Toast.
my boys loved it! however, it did stick to my non-stick griddle so I'll have to spray the pan next time. I used my immersion blender and the cocoa blended perfectly without any lumps.
I followed the recipe, except I used chocolate syrup for the cocoa. It turned out delicious! Freezes well. Will make again.
